categories.name: Bitterballen
categories.note: A selection from two lists. Which one is best is a matter of taste.

categories.name: Fine dining
categories.note: Tasting menus cost about €100-250 per person. Book at least two weeks ahead. Dress code: smart casual.

categories.name: Markets
categories.note: Hours come from various sources. Check them before you go.

items.name: De Koffieschenkerij
items.text: Daily 9am-6pm. Coffee and cake in the former sacristy of the Oude Kerk, with a hidden courtyard.

items.name: Café Winkel 43
items.text: Famous for its apple pie, with a terrace on the market square by the Noorderkerk. No reservations, just grab a seat.

items.name: Rudi's Original Stroopwafels
items.text: Freshly baked stroopwafels from a food truck on the market, made to a secret recipe from Gouda. Not a tourist shop with balloons.

items.name: De Laatste Kruimel
items.text: Cosy café for breakfast and lunch with sandwiches, quiche and homemade lemonade. Small terrace by the canal.

items.name: Café Americain
items.text: A classic grand café in the American Hotel, with an Art Deco interior from 1928, Tiffany lamps and a terrace on the square. Coffee, lunch, afternoon tea and dinner.

items.name: The Kitchen at De Bijenkorf
items.text: At the top of the department store. Coffee with a slice of cake, with views over the city and a small terrace. Check opening hours beforehand, sources differ.

items.name: Restaurant Moeders
items.text: Mon-Fri 5-10pm, Sat-Sun 4.30-10pm. Stamppot, braised beef and French toast. Book well ahead.

items.name: De Blauwe Hollander
items.text: Big portions of stamppot.

items.name: Heertje Friet
items.text: Near the Nine Streets. In my view the best fries in town: fresh and hand-cut, with the sauce of your choice (joppie, oorlog, frietsaus). Seating, also outside by the canal. Daily 11am-8pm.

items.name: FEBO
items.text: The classic snack wall for late nights: croquette, frikandel or satay croquette from the little hatch. Open late into the night, check the hours beforehand.

items.name: Stubbe's Haring
items.text: By the Haarlemmersluis. A herring stall for more than a hundred years. Hollandse Nieuwe with onion and pickled gherkin, or in a bun. Stand and eat, no seating. Check opening hours beforehand.

items.name: Vishuisje Simon en Simon
items.text: A small herring stall on the bridge over the Prinsengracht, run by a father and son. A good herring sandwich according to visitors and locals. Check opening hours beforehand.

items.name: Proeflokaal A. van Wees
items.text: Historic tasting house with bitterballen of wild boar, tiger prawn, classic beef and a vegetarian mushroom and aubergine one. Also the place to taste very good jenever.

items.name: Café Luxembourg
items.text: Famous café with three prize-winning bitterballen: beef, shrimp and Dutch cheese.

items.name: Eetsalon Van Dobben
items.text: Snack bar since 1945, which also supplies bitterballen to other cafés.

items.name: Café de Tuin
items.text: Brown café in the Jordaan with the traditional beef ragout bitterbal.

items.name: Flore
items.text: In Hotel De L'Europe, on the Amstel. Formerly Bord'Eau. Chef Bas van Kranen, two Michelin stars.

items.name: Vinkeles
items.text: Two Michelin stars in a sunken 18th-century bakery. Dinner only, Tue-Sat 7-10pm.

items.name: RIJKS
items.text: Inside the Rijksmuseum. Chef Joris Bijdendijk was named best chef of the year in 2025.

items.name: De Kas
items.text: In Frankendael. Michelin star and green star, organic, in a greenhouse.

items.name: Lars
items.text: In the Houthavens. Michelin star.

items.name: Showw
items.text: Michelin star.

items.name: More at De L'Europe
items.text: Hoofdstad Brasserie (lighter), Hèt Terras (large terrace on the Amstel), Freddy's Bar and Chapter 1896 (cocktails with a view of the Amstel).

items.name: The Duchess
items.text: Opposite Hotel W. French and Italian brasserie (€€€) in a former banking hall in Belle Époque style, with dark marble, chandeliers and an open kitchen. Famous for its beef Wellington. Mon-Thu 5pm-1am, Fri-Sat noon-2am, Sun noon-1am. Reservations on +31 20 811 3322. Afternoon tea at weekends.

items.name: De Silveren Spiegel
items.text: Creative French cooking (€€€) in two step-gabled houses from 1614, with an open fireplace, candlelight and plenty of natural wine. Listed in the Michelin Guide, without a star. Tue-Thu 6-11pm, Fri-Sat 12.30-10pm, closed Sun and Mon.

items.name: Ron Gastrobar
items.text: Near the Vondelpark. Gastrobar by chef Ron Blaauw: quality without the formality, with small dishes to share, aged steaks and fish.

items.name: Toscanini
items.text: In the Jordaan. Authentic Italian since 1985, with an open kitchen, seasonal regional dishes and home-baked bread. Hard to get a table, so book well ahead.

items.name: Mr. Porter
items.text: In the penthouse of Hotel W. Steakhouse and cocktail bar with dry-aged beef and a rooftop terrace overlooking the Dam and the Nine Streets. Reviewers praise the grass-fed steaks, the zucchini carpaccio and the chocolate fondant.

items.name: Pllek
items.text: Amsterdam-Noord, near the NDSM shipyard (by ferry across the IJ). Organic and sustainable restaurant in a raw industrial setting, with a city beach and views over the IJ.

items.name: De Belhamel
items.text: On the corner with the Herengracht. Seasonal Dutch cooking with Mediterranean influences, in an Art Nouveau interior with canal views. A quiet spot away from the crowds.

items.name: Hannekes Boom
items.text: Right by Central Station. A rustic café built from reclaimed materials with a large waterside terrace and local, organic products.

items.name: Kartika
items.text: Rijsttafel, for decades, vegetarian options too.

items.name: Mama Makan
items.text: Indonesian classics, modern style.

items.name: Restaurant Max
items.text: Rijsttafel in the canal ring with traditional, fusion and milder versions. Known for its friendly service and a wine list that suits Indonesian food.

items.name: Tempo Doeloe
items.text: One of the best-known rijsttafels in town, spicy and with white tablecloths. Dinner only.

items.name: Van 't Spit
items.text: Also at Frans Halsstraat 42. Spit-roast chicken.

items.name: Bierfabriek
items.text: Piri-piri chicken and ribs.

items.name: Ladybird Fried Chicken
items.text: In De Pijp.

items.name: Kip 'n Drip (KID)
items.text: In De Pijp. Said by many to be the best chicken burger in Amsterdam.

items.name: Chris Kip
items.text: Since 1928, organic.

items.name: In 't Aepjen
items.text: One of the two wooden houses left in Amsterdam (c. 1475-1550). Jenever and beer. Sun-Thu noon-1am, Fri-Sat noon-3am.

items.name: Bird
items.text: Authentic Thai since 1998, often with a queue at the door.

items.name: Fo Guang Shan He Hua Temple
items.text: The largest Chinese-style temple on the European mainland. Free entry, shoes off. Tue-Sat noon-5pm, Sun 10am-5pm, closed Mon.

items.name: Trees
items.text: Atmospheric restaurant in a historic corner building.

items.name: Amsterdamsche Vishandel Anno 1938
items.text: Classic fishmonger.

items.name: Fromagerie Abraham Kef
items.text: Cheese shop since the 1950s, also wine and delicacies. Often a queue.

items.name: De Amsterdamse Muis
items.text: Vintage décor, Delft blue and gifts. Tue-Sat 11am-6pm.

items.name: Antiekcentrum
items.text: In the Jordaan. The largest indoor antiques market in the Netherlands, 55 dealers. Free entry.

items.name: Alladin's Notenhoek
items.text: Oud-West (not in the centre). Family business where the former queen bought her nuts.

items.name: Tony's Chocolonely Super Store
items.text: Near the Damrak, about a 5-minute walk from Centraal Station. Daily 10am-7pm, free entry. Make your own bar, taste the bars and learn about the cocoa problem. Small, often a queue, steep stairs and not wheelchair accessible.

items.name: Albert Cuypmarkt
items.text: De Pijp. Mon-Sat 9am-6pm. With 260 stalls the largest daily market in Europe: vegetables, clothes, flowers, herring and fresh stroopwafels.

items.name: Noordermarkt
items.text: Jordaan. Mon 9am-1pm (flea market and fabrics), Sat 9am-4pm (organic farmers' market).

items.name: Waterlooplein
items.text: Mon-Sat during the day. Flea market with vintage clothes, antiques and bric-a-brac.

items.name: Bloemenmarkt (flower market)
items.text: Mon-Sat about 9am-5.30pm, Sun 11am-5.30pm.

items.name: Dappermarkt
items.text: Oost. Mon-Sat 9am-5pm. Food from all over the world, clothes and household goods.

items.name: Ten Katemarkt
items.text: Oud-West. Mon-Sat.

items.name: Lindengracht
items.text: Jordaan. Saturday only.

items.name: Westerstraat
items.text: Jordaan. Monday only. Fabrics, clothes and shoes.

items.name: Nieuwmarkt
items.text: Sat organic farmers' market, Sun antiques market from May to September.

items.name: IJ-Hallen
items.text: Noord. Flea market, one weekend a month.

items.name: Poffertjes at the market
items.text: According to one source the Amsterdamse Poffertjes stall stands at the Noordermarkt (Sat) and sometimes at the Albert Cuypmarkt (Mon, Tue, Thu). Check this.

items.name: KattenKabinet
items.text: Art museum about cats in a canal house from 1667, with real cats. Tue-Sun noon-5pm.

items.name: Hortus Botanicus
items.text: Botanical garden since 1638, with a butterfly house. Daily 10am-5pm.

items.name: Museum Van Loon
items.text: Canal house from 1672 with a garden and coach house. Wed-Sun 10am-5pm, closed Mon and Tue.

items.name: Foam
items.text: Photography museum, right next to Van Loon. Daily 10am-6pm, Thu-Fri until 9pm.

items.name: Rijksmuseum
items.text: Daily 9am-5pm. Don't miss the public bike passage under the museum.

items.name: Entrepotdok
items.text: 19th-century warehouses, now homes and houseboats, next to Artis. Always open and free.

items.name: NDSM-werf
items.text: Former shipyard in Amsterdam-Noord. Take the ferry (line F3) from Centraal Station: free for pedestrians and cyclists, at least twice an hour.

items.name: Reguliersdwarsstraat
items.text: Near Rembrandtplein. Well-known LGBTQ+ street, home to the first gay bar in 1963.

items.name: Picasso in the Vondelpark
items.text: The sculpture "Figure découpée / l'Oiseau" (1965), known locally as "the Fish". Picasso gave it to the city for the park's 100th anniversary, out of friendship with Willem Sandberg.

items.name: A'DAM Lookout
items.text: Observation tower with 360-degree views, reached by the free ferry from Centraal Station. The highlight is the Over The Edge swing: you swing over the edge of the roof at almost 100 metres.

items.name: Swimming at the Marineterrein
items.text: Swim in the inner harbour with views of the Maritime Museum and NEMO, right in the city centre. Free to access.

items.name: Kuuma Sauna
items.text: By the piers. Wood-fired sauna on the water that you rent by the time slot, alone or with a group. Book at kuuma.nl.

items.name: Pension Homeland
items.text: Own brewery with more than ten house-brewed beers, plus café, restaurant and a sunny terrace, in the former officers' mess.

items.name: ENTR VR Museum
items.text: Right by the OBA library and Centraal Station. The first VR museum in the Netherlands. In "Amsterdam 1652" you walk with other visitors through a recreated 17th-century Amsterdam. Tickets from €18, book ahead.

items.name: Proeflokaal 't Arendsnest
items.text: A café serving only Dutch beer: 52 Dutch beers on tap plus bottles, from witbier to stout and IPA.

items.name: Coffeeshop Siberië
items.text: Coffeeshop in a converted garage with candles, big wooden tables, games and a live DJ at weekends. 18+ only.

items.name: Het Stenen Hoofd
items.text: A former harbour pier from 1902, now a public park on the IJ and a popular spot to walk your dog. Freely accessible.

items.name: Boom Chicago
items.text: American comedy with a Dutch twist: improv and sketches in English. Check show days at boomchicago.nl.

items.name: De Hollandsche Manege
items.text: A neoclassical riding hall from 1882 with a public café-restaurant where you can watch the riders.

items.name: VROG
items.text: Indoor play space for trampolining, parkour and dance in a former car tunnel near Waterlooplein. Fun with children, including toddlers.

items.name: NEMO Science Museum
items.text: A science museum for young and old with experiments, workshops and a rooftop square with views over the city.

items.name: Klimmuur Amsterdam Centraal
items.text: A large climbing hall near Central Station with boulder walls and routes (8 and 16 metres). For children and adults, with taster lessons.

items.name: Paradiso
items.text: Concerts and parties in a former church near Leidseplein.

items.name: Bitterzoet
items.text: Club and stage for every kind of music.

items.name: Tuschinski
items.text: A beautiful Art Deco cinema, worth a look inside.

items.name: The Movies
items.text: Small Art Deco cinema with dark lacquered wood, said by the tourist board to be the oldest in Amsterdam.

items.name: Café Papeneiland
items.text: On the corner of Brouwersgracht. One of the oldest cafés in the city (1642), with Delft tiles and famous for its apple pie.

items.name: Café 't Smalle
items.text: A traditional brown café in a former distillery from 1780, with a canal-side terrace.

items.name: Café de Prins
items.text: A cosy café near the Westerkerk, known for its candles and poffertjes.

items.name: Marineterrein and the VOC ship
items.text: On the water at the Marineterrein, with the replica of the VOC ship Amsterdam next to the Maritime Museum nearby.

items.name: Brouwersgracht
items.text: At the corner of Herengracht and Prinsengracht. Three canals meet here.

items.name: Damrak
items.text: In the late afternoon. Lovely light on the facades.
